The idea that shame isn't a good motivator is a very modern bullshit idea that's mostly come from that Oprah "Feel good\Positivity" culture. If shame lead to suicide it would have been weeded out through natural selection. Shame is always there at the back of a person's mind just in case they do something that is not to a standard they or their peers expect of them. It's not overwhelming. It's the same fear that makes you double check you've switched off the gas before you leave the house. You're not paranoid or OCD. You get a flash in your mind of what might happen if you do a shitty job, so you double check to make sure it's done right. Then you go about your day.

If you've ever gotten to a place 5 minutes earlier because you wanted to make sure the person you were meeting didn't think you were unreliable or a flake then you understand the role shame can play in maintaining a good standard and living with strong values.

Find anybody who does anything to a high standard and then ask them to lower their standard, and you'll see that flash of fear of shame and disgust creep across their face. NO FUCKING WAY. "I keep my kitchen CLEAN! I keep my body in good shape! I make the best product I can for my customers and I won't settle for anything less!"

Shaming is the "ying" to the "yang" of taking pride in a high standard.
